dedupe_keys.name: 33 cfr part 162 us inland waterways navigation regulations ecfr

description: Part 162 of Title 33 of the US Code of Federal Regulations, Inland Waterways Navigation Regulations, sets the waterway-specific navigation rules administered by the US Coast Guard, and the Electronic Code of Federal Regulations (eCFR) publishes its current text. Coverage: general provisions and definitions, then sections for named waterways across the country: the Chesapeake and Delaware Canal, waterways tributary to the Atlantic and to the Gulf south of Chesapeake Bay, the Mississippi below the Ohio, the Arkansas River system, the Ohio River at Louisville, the Missouri River, Great Lakes harbours and connecting waters from Lake Huron to Lake Erie (with communications, traffic, anchorage and speed rules), the Columbia and Willamette rivers, Puget Sound, Alaskan narrows and San Juan harbour, plus restricted areas such as seaplane zones and reserve fleet sites. Format and access: HTML on eCFR, with a versioner API that returns the structure as JSON and point-in-time full text as XML. Licence and cost: US federal regulations are public domain and free. Caveats: the eCFR is an editorial compilation, not the official legal edition, and local notices can add temporary rules. The speed, traffic and anchorage rules can be encoded as constraints in vessel traffic and waterway network flow simulations. It relates to the Inland Electronic Navigational Charts and ES-TRIN in the catalogue.
